subject: Private Deploy — EU/APAC egress segmentation & peering review
messages:
From: Tom Blake <tom.blake@acme.com>

Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, Sofia Petrov <sofia.petrov@dg-cloud.io>

Subject: Initial: Acme private deploy constraints — EU keys and APAC edge peering

Hi Kim / Marissa,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is a short requirements doc for the Acme private deployment. High-level constraints:
- All customer PII + model inputs must remain resident in the EU (no cross-border writes).
- Key material (KMS) must be provisioned and controlled by Acme in EU-only KMS. Redwood can have a public key for envelope encryption but cannot hold primary keys outside EU.
- APAC office needs a low-latency edge for inference (on-prem proxy/orchestrator) with an eventual warm-standby in APAC but primary custody in EU.
- During partial network failures we need an explicit degraded-mode flow that keeps data in EU but can still service inference if the APAC edge loses connectivity.

Questions for the review:
1) Can Redwood support regional egress isolation (APAC edge cannot egress to anything outside APAC except to authenticated EU control-plane endpoints)?
2) How do we handle KMS/cryptographic separation and failover without violating residency?
3) What peering and NAT/egress model do you recommend for per-tenant containment?

Attachment: [attachment: acme-mvp-requirements.pdf (application/pdf, 220 KB)]

Tom Blake
Head of Infrastructure, Acme, Inc.

Subject: Re: Initial: Acme private deploy constraints — EU keys and APAC edge peering

Tom — thanks for the clear brief and the attachment. I skimmed the requirements and sketched two high-level options; I'll summarize and attach a quick diagram.

Option A — EU-primary, APAC edge with controlled peering (preferred):
- Data-at-rest and primary model hosting remain in EU clusters.
- APAC on-prem edge acts as reverse-proxy + KV-cache (no local persistent writes beyond cache).
- Egress: APAC edge only allowed to call a small set of EU control-plane endpoints (mutual TLS + per-tenant ACLs).
- KMS: customer-managed EU-only KMS for master keys. Redwood holds ephemeral encryption keys (public part) for envelope wrapping; actual DEKs are wrapped by Acme's EU KMS.

Option B — Split custody with selective replication (higher complexity):
- Replicate encrypted snapshots to APAC standby under strict export controls and customer consent.
- Failover requires manual approval and audit trail.

Network / peering notes:
- Use route-based peering where APAC edge announces a private prefix to the customer VPC and we apply egress NAT and ACLs there.
- Split-horizon DNS to ensure service endpoints resolve to EU endpoints unless session-affinity is established to APAC edge.
- BGP tiebreak policy + health probes to detect split-brain and prevent accidental cross-border writes.

I've attached a simple diagram: [attachment: network-diagram-kp-v1.png (image/png, 120 KB)]. Next step: pick one option and we can draft a formal playbook (prechecks, KMS handoff, canary tests).

Propose a short design review on Thursday morning (30m). Are you available?

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Kim — this is helpful, thanks. A few clarifications / concerns:
- KMS: we cannot export DEKs or snapshots outside the EU at any time. Envelope encryption where the wrapping key is in EU KMS is acceptable, but any automated replication that results in unwrapped DEKs outside the EU is a blocker.
- SSO: Acme is on Okta. We want SAML-based break-glass to be tested during failover runs.
- Performance: APAC teams want <60ms p95 for inference. If APAC only has a reverse-proxy + cache model, can you quantify expected delta vs full APAC-hosted inference?

Sofia (cc) will provide our network peering contact and the preferred maintenance windows.

Tom

Subject: Re: Initial: Acme private deploy constraints — EU keys and APAC edge peering

Tom — good catches. Quick answers and a proposed path forward:

KMS / encryption:
- We'll implement envelope encryption where Acme's EU KMS holds the wrapping keys. Redwood will never have access to unwrapped DEKs outside EU.
- For warm standby we propose encrypted snapshots (ciphertext only) replicated to APAC; any action that requires unwrapping must call into the EU KMS (synchronous RPC) and be logged for audit. If the EU KMS is unreachable, the APAC standby will run in read-only cache/degraded inference mode.

SSO / break-glass:
- We support SAML for admin login and will add a documented break-glass flow. We recommend a scheduled failover drill that exercises SSO flows including the Okta break-glass.

Performance tradeoffs:
- Reverse-proxy + KV-cache approach typically adds ~12-40ms p95 depending on model size and cache hit-rate. If Acme needs sub-60ms p95 consistently, we should consider a small quantized model variant in APAC as a true warm-standby (model weights encrypted at rest, DEKs wrapped by EU KMS). This increases ops complexity but meets performance.

Proposed next steps:
1) Design review (Thu 30m) — agree on Option A vs Option B.
2) Security playbook: KMS handoff, audit events, allowed control-plane endpoints.
3) Network plan: peering CIDR list, BGP health-checks, split-horizon DNS entries.
4) Canary: synthetic traffic from APAC to validate p95 and cache hit-rates.

Attachment: [attachment: redwood-egress-segmentation-proposal-v1.pdf (application/pdf, 400 KB)].

We can run the design review Thursday 09:00 UTC — Ying? (Sofia: is this OK for your peering team to attend?)

—Kim
